body.content: Key tension: SRC_008 attributes the nocturnal UHI to low albedo causing greater daytime absorption, but this is incomplete — the albedo difference explains daytime heat storage, not why the city stays warm at NIGHT. The nocturnal gap is about differential cooling rates (urban slow vs. rural fast), not differential daytime heating. The covering principle must explain why the city cools more slowly after sunset. Candidate mechanisms: (1) thermal mass / heat capacity release, (2) sky view factor radiative trapping, (3) anthropogenic heat, (4) moisture deficit / evapotranspiration. The question demands a SINGLE mechanism for cross-city variation, forcing a choice among these.
body.possible_next_move: Propose a simulation that isolates sky view factor from thermal mass by holding material properties constant and varying canyon geometry.
body.unfinished: Which single mechanism is most defensible as the cross-city modulator? Sky view factor is geometric and clean, but thermal mass is more physically fundamental. Need to disentangle.
body.why_keep_this: Clarifies the logical distinction between daytime absorption (albedo) and nocturnal retention (cooling rate), which is essential for the correct answer.
